title: BREAKING: 11 Dems Vote Against Hakeem Jeffries for Speaker
author: Andrew Perez

Despite his [unpopularity](https://www.newsweek.com/jeffries-approval-rating-
worse-than-mike-johnson-as-democratic-voters-rebel-12679163) among the
American public, Hakeem Jeffries received a resounding vote of confidence from
most House Democrats on Wednesday. He is now on track to be the first Black
speaker of the House next year.

Only 11 Democrats voted against Jeffries, while two did not vote. The vote was
done on a secret ballot. However, seven incoming progressive freshmen -
Darializa Avila Chevalier, Adam Hamawy, Melat Kiros, Donavan McKinney, Chris
Rabb, and Claire Valdez -
[released](https://x.com/allymutnick/status/2123076132677484763?a=bi76_yLzhn-
JZmlwjCs&s=20) a statement indicating they voted no on Wednesday.

"Whether on Medicare for All, stopping ICE terror, getting money out of
politics, or ending the genocide in Gaza, our constituents sent us to Congress
with a mandate on these issues," they said. "We have worked to secure
commitments from Leader Jeffries in good-faith conversations. While we have
seen meaningful progress, there is still work to be done to ensure that the
direction our party takes this coming Congress reflects what our constituents
are demanding of leadership."

Incoming Rep. [Don Leonard](https://zeteo.com/p/don-leonard-israel-jeffries)
also
[indicated](https://x.com/mkraju/status/2123076548500594845?a=8miV7pCQOvNXyPkYdu4&s=20)
that he would be voting against Jeffries. A spokesperson for incoming Rep.
Frederick Haynes [said](https://x.com/allymutnick/status/2123111201534017685)
he was ill and missed the vote, but intended to vote no on Jeffries.

Democrats won full control of Congress two weeks ago, and the biggest House
majority in decades, as voters repudiated Donald Trump and his disastrous,
failed war in Iran. Ever since then, Democratic congressional offices have
[reportedly](https://www.axios.com/2026/11/06/jeffries-speaker-democrats-
house-calls-petition) been "inundated" with calls and emails from constituents
calling on them to oppose Jeffries for speaker.

Progressives and several incoming lawmakers had been pushing for policy
concessions and commitments from Jeffries. They did not apparently receive
any.

While Democrats' Senate leader, Chuck Schumer, is facing a challenge from
Senator Chris Van Hollen, no lawmakers stepped up to run against Jeffries in
the House.

Jeffries's politics are not an obvious fit with the evolving Dem base. While
Jeffries, the House minority leader since 2023, was a longtime supporter of
Medicare for All, he publicly
[opposed](https://truthout.org/articles/jeffries-says-he-opposes-medicare-for-
all-which-would-save-114k-lives-yearly/) it this summer. Jeffries - like his
Senate counterpart, Schumer - is a [fervent
supporter](https://x.com/DropSiteNews/status/2122892769773355025?a=l-ENJ4mirDNld8577YY&s=20)
of Israel.

In recent days, Jeffries moved to shore up support by evincing a mild leftward
shift. He [endorsed](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/congress/jeffries-
endorses-lowering-medicare-age-adding-benefits-universal-cove-rcna609843)
efforts to lower the Medicare eligibility age and expand benefits - two ideas
recently pushed by Bernie Sanders that Democrats previously pursued during Joe
Biden's presidency. Jeffries also [called](https://www.haaretz.com/us-
news/2026-11-17/ty-article-magazine/.premium/hakeem-jeffries-wants-dramatic-
change-on-israel-what-does-that-mean/000001a1-e682-d381-ade5-efe33b5a0000) for
"dramatic change" in Israel, Gaza, and the West Bank.

But progressives had pushed Jeffries to pledge to hold a vote on legislation
to end military aid and weapons sales to Israel. They did not extract such
concessions in the lead-up to the vote.

"We have not succeeded in getting any commitments yet on Gaza or Israel,"
[said](https://x.com/DropSiteNews/status/2122892769773355025?a=l-ENJ4mirDNld8577YY&s=20)
Rep. Ro Khanna Tuesday night.
